title: Contributor onboarding, RFC lifecycle, and graceful deprecation checklist for UI primitives
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create a single, pragmatic playbook that bundles contributor onboarding, an RFC lifecycle for visual primitives (tokens, buttons, tables, charts), and a clear graceful-deprecation process. This ticket will produce the canonical guide, checklist artifacts (for PRs, design reviews, and engineering rollouts), and implement two short-term automation helpers (lint warnings for deprecated tokens and a documentation banner pattern). The goal is to reduce surprise regressions, speed up contributor flow, and ensure safe backwards-compatible transitions for clients of the design system.
background: We have ad-hoc contribution notes scattered across docs and intermittent deprecation notices. Recent regressions (color token rename in runtime-1.18 rollout) caused downstream layout flickers for two client teams. Designers, engineers, and PMs lack a unified workflow for proposing changes, collecting cross-functional signoff, and migrating consumers. This playbook standardizes how RFCs are written, how deprecations are communicated, and what automation/guardrails are required for low-friction adoption.
proposal_summary: Deliver a one-page contributor onboarding with linked RFC template; an RFC lifecycle doc describing review gates (design, accessibility, engineering, product); a deprecation lifecycle with timelines, automation, and migration helpers; and a small set of implementation steps (docs banner, lint rules, changelog entry conventions). Prioritize tokens and small UI primitives (buttons, tables, charts) for the first rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical contributor onboarding doc published in the design system docs site
RFC template and explicit lifecycle (Draft -> Review -> Approved -> Implement -> Deprecate -> Remove) documented with responsibilities
Deprecation checklist published with minimum notice windows for tokens (45 days) and components (60 days), plus automatic warnings in Storybook and code linting
Two automation helpers merged: lint rule that flags deprecated token usage, docs banner component that can be toggled for deprecated items
Migration notes and codemod examples for the most-used tokens and button variants
At least one downstream team (Payments) confirms the migration path and signs off in comments
deprecation_policy_highlights: Soft deprecation period: tokens = 45 days, components = 60 days by default
Deprecation stages: Announce (public changelog + email), Soft-deprecate (lint warnings + docs banner), Hard-deprecate (remove from library after buffer and confirmed migrations)
Compatibility guarantee: patch releases will not break public tokens; breaking changes require deprecation workflow and migration helpers
Exceptions: security fixes or critical performance regressions can accelerate removal with cross-team emergency process
rfc_lifecycle: Author creates RFC using template and links Figma/PRD and example usage
Design review for visual and accessibility checks; tag @design-exec for major token changes
Engineering review for runtime/compatibility (serving runtime implications like KV caching or kernel selection must be noted)
PM review for product impact and release coordination (Dedicated/Private customers may need extra lead time)
Public comment window (7 business days) before final approval
Post-approval: assign implementation owner, create engineering ticket(s) with migration checklist
implementation_notes: Add Storybook banner for deprecated components with link to migration notes
Ship ESLint rule (or TypeScript transformer) that emits warnings on deprecated token usage; include autofix patterns when safe
Create codemod examples for token renames and primary button variant replacements
Add 'deprecated' metadata field to component props in the design system repo for programmatic detection
Console: add deprecation flag UI to component detail pages for developer docs
migration_support: Migration docs with before/after snippets and performance considerations
Office hours / drop-in sessions scheduled during first two weeks of soft-deprecation
Priority support for enterprise Dedicated customers to coordinate migration windows
